column1: # How apps/web/gods-eye-view differs from upstream bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.
# This copy is upstream at the base commit below, plus the license header
# //tools/license:add gives each file, plus exactly the changes listed here,
# proves it; `sync` moves the base and rewrites the line itself. Paths are
# relative to apps/web/gods-eye-view; a path ending in / covers a directory of
# files upstream does not have. See upstream/README.md.
# change: added (only here), modified (both, but different), deleted (only upstream)

column3: tree
why
Legacy local-context filter (superseded for repo-root builds by Dockerfile.dockerignore). Upstream ships its own for its dev container; this copy keeps the monorepo's.
Bazel targets. Named BUILD.bazel because a file named BUILD collides with upstream's build/ directory on case-insensitive file systems.
The production image, published to GHCR and deployed by gitops/argocd. Upstream now ships its own, for its dev container; this copy keeps the monorepo's.
Repo-root Docker build context filter for the production Dockerfile, whitelisting workspace manifests and apps/web/gods-eye-view/.
Monorepo code ownership.
Backstage catalog entry, as every app in this repository has, so the developer portal lists the app with its owner and source.
Points compose build at the monorepo root context with apps/web/gods-eye-view/Dockerfile.

The production server the image runs. Upstream serves its /api routes from its Vite dev server; this serves dist/ and mounts upstream's own provider plugins through their configurePreviewServer hooks, as `vite preview` does, so upstream's routes reach production with each sync.
Bazel entry point for upstream's test runner: puts a real node ahead of the rules_js shim, which upstream's spawned scripts cannot use.
Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/build_military_names.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:build_military_names`).
Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/dev_helpers.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:dev_cctv`).
Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/dev_helpers.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:dev_fresh`).
Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/dev_helpers.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:dev_secure`).
Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/opensky_import_client.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:opensky_import_client`).
Declares the crates the Rust ports in scripts/src use (serde, serde_json, image) as a member of the root Cargo workspace, which the Bazel @crates hub and Cargo.lock resolve from.

Native Rust ports of the helper scripts (`build-military-names`, `verify-cesium-assets`, `opensky-import-client`, `dev-cctv`, `dev-fresh`, `dev-secure`), of the imagery CLI tools `pano-pinhole`, `sat-ortho`, `streetview-headings` and `streetview-panorama` (complete: fetching through curl, image decode and JPEG encode, same file names; `tool_io.rs` holds what they share), a partial port of `cesium-render` (argument parsing and geometry only, so `tools/cesium-render.mjs` remains the working tool), the CelesTrak mirror (`tle_mirror.rs`, a standard-library-only crate of its own, which .github/workflows/gods-eye-view-tle-mirror.yaml builds with plain rustc and runs every 6 hours from GitHub's runners, because connections from the homelab to celestrak.org time out; `:tle_mirror_test` holds its groups to the client's and its URL to the server's), and architecture/format boundary checks (`check-import-directions` with the module analysis it uses, and `check-package-boundaries`, both complete and run by `npm run check:boundaries`; `check-format-scope`), plus their unit tests, which include the cases of upstream's `importDirections.test.mjs` and `packageBoundaries.test.mjs`.

Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/check_import_directions.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:check_import_directions`, gated on the live tree by `:check_import_directions_test`). A sync that changes upstream's rules ports them there.
Only `check-import-directions.mjs` used it; `analyze_module` in `scripts/src/check_import_directions.rs` is its port.

Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/check_package_boundaries.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:check_package_boundaries`, gated on the live tree by `:check_package_boundaries_test`). It walks each group's import graph instead of running a Vite build; a sync that changes upstream's rules ports them there.

Tested `check-import-directions.mjs` and `module-analysis.mjs`, which are not in this copy; its cases run against the Rust port in `check_import_directions::tests` and `tests::module_analysis_parses_imports_and_browser_globals` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:scripts_test`).
Tested `check-package-boundaries.mjs`, which is not in this copy; its cases run against the Rust port in `check_package_boundaries::tests` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:scripts_test`).
Drops the five boundary-check files above, which are not in this copy.
Its import direction gates section names the Rust targets that `npm run check:boundaries` runs here.
Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/pano_pinhole.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:pano_pinhole`).
Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/sat_ortho.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:sat_ortho`).
Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/streetview_headings.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:streetview_headings`).
Superseded by the native Rust port in `scripts/src/streetview_panorama.rs` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:streetview_panorama`).
The four imagery tools above are Rust programs here: their sections run them with `bazel run //apps/web/gods-eye-view:<tool> --` and say where `.env`, `--outdir` and `--input` resolve.
Its Tooling Snapshot names the Rust targets of the four imagery tools, whose tools/*.mjs are not in this copy.

Drops the case for tools/streetview-headings.mjs's key loader, which is not in this copy; the same cases run against the Rust port in `streetview_headings::tests` (`//apps/web/gods-eye-view:scripts_test`).
Pins HOME_VIEW and HOME_START_VIEW, the landing view src/camera.js adds.
Skips legacy bash launcher tests once `scripts/dev-cctv.sh` and `scripts/dev-fresh.sh` are superseded by `//apps/web/gods-eye-view:scripts_test`.
Skips legacy `scripts/dev-fresh.sh` source checks once `dev-fresh.sh` is superseded by `//apps/web/gods-eye-view:scripts_test`, while keeping the `read-dotenv-value.mjs` tests active.
Skips the legacy `scripts/dev-fresh.sh` launcher subtest once `dev-fresh.sh` is superseded by `//apps/web/gods-eye-view:scripts_test`.
Drops `scripts/dev-fresh.sh` from `DOCUMENTED_KEYS` once `dev-fresh.sh` is superseded by `scripts/src/dev_helpers.rs`.
The monorepo's end-to-end suite against the production server.

Native Rust port of the E2E test suite (262 tests across 5 tiers: feature, boundary, combination, scenario, adversarial). Runs hermetically in the Bazel sandbox in milliseconds without spawning python3, node, or bash subprocesses.

:server_test, which boots server.mjs from the Dockerfile's runtime layout and checks it serves every route upstream mounts for `vite preview`, none of the dev-only ones, and the same-site gate on the paid ones.
This tracking: the tool, its tests, this list and the sync brief.
The monorepo is one pnpm workspace; pnpm-lock.yaml at the repository root is the lockfile.
Upstream's CI, which never runs here; Dependabot bumps its action pins with the rest of the repository's.

Browser build at target es2022 with ES-module workers: satellite.js 7, at the monorepo's one version, ships an Emscripten wasm build that spawns a module worker and uses top-level await, which Vite's defaults (iife workers, es2020) cannot bundle (#3581).

Dependencies at the monorepo's one version (cesium, sharp, satellite.js 7, vite 8, happy-dom and its global registrator 21, since 20.14.6 carries GHSA-834v-8h66-3h79 and GHSA-c8p4-j97h-3vg8 and the osv-scan gate refuses new advisories, @vitejs/plugin-vue 6 for vite 8; build/vite.js and src/data/infrastructure.test.mjs carry what the last two need); @cesium/core, @cesium/engine and @cesium/widgets declared, which upstream's tests import and npm hoists but pnpm does not; ws a runtime dependency, since upstream's AIS provider requires it at run time and the image installs dependencies only; `start` runs server.mjs; `dev:secure`, `opensky:import` and `check:boundaries` run the Rust ports through `bazel run`, since their scripts are not in this copy.
Tries a mirror of CelesTrak's groups first when CELESTRAK_TLE_MIRROR_URL is set, then CelesTrak: production cannot reach celestrak.org (see scripts/src/tle_mirror.rs).
Starts on HOME_START_VIEW (Irvine, CA) by default instead of the whole planet; a host's own startView still wins.
HOME_VIEW and HOME_START_VIEW: one constant for the landing city, which controls.js starts on.
git grep exits 128 in the Bazel sandbox, which has no .git, as well as 1 for no match.
The stalled requests hold a timer, so node does not exit before the abort under Bazel (upstream's own keep-alive covers only one of them), and an already-aborted signal rejects at once.
The hung upstream holds a timer, so node does not exit before the overall budget's unref'd timer fires under Bazel, which cancelled this test and every one after it.
The stalled lookups hold a timer, so node does not exit before the abort under Bazel, and an already-aborted signal rejects at once.

Replaces vite-plugin-cesium's asset copy with a dereferencing one, because the rules_js fs patches reject its walk over pnpm's symlinks and the bundle shipped without dist/cesium; materializes index.html in place during Bazel builds so Rolldown's native canonicalize stays inside darwin-sandbox.
Asserts the consumer build stays in src/data and src/sources rather than an exact module list: Vite 8, at the monorepo's one version, chunks the build differently from upstream's Vite 6 (#3601).
The Bazel test sandbox has no .git, so `git ls-files` fails and the i18n catalog tests could not list the sources; it falls back to walking the tree for the same pathspecs.
Expects this copy's Dockerfile, whose entry point is the production server (server.mjs), not upstream's dev launcher.
Vite 8, at the monorepo's one version, words its refusal 'This host ("x") is not allowed'; the match accepts both wordings.

Node 22 (this copy's image and Bazel toolchain) decodes windows-1252 as Latin-1, leaving the feed's 0x96 a control character; Node 24 gives the en dash. The expected title follows the runtime's decoder.
The hanging fetch holds a timer until its abort: AbortSignal.timeout's timer is unref'd, so under Bazel node exits before the deadline fires.
STARRY_SKY_CESIUM_VERSION names the cesium release the repository resolves (package.json pins it at the monorepo version), so it follows that version, not upstream's.

SCREEN_MODULATION_CESIUM_VERSION names the cesium release the repository resolves (package.json pins it at the monorepo version), so it follows that version, not upstream's. Its GPU revalidation at that version is still owed.
Vite 8, at the monorepo's one version, refuses a disallowed Host before any plugin middleware runs, so that refusal carries no API headers; the test checks only its status.
Server-side Sentry error monitoring and diagnostics endpoint (/api/diagnostics/sentry-test).
Unit tests for server-side Sentry initialization, error capture, and diagnostics plugin.

Initializes client-side Sentry error monitoring and captures startup failures.
Adds styles for key-setup-sentry-test diagnostic button.
